text.approach: Ferry/floatplane to Stehekin (no road access), then the Company Creek Trail roughly 3 miles to a point below Tupshin's west side. Leave the trail and scramble up White Goat Mountain's west slopes through dense brush, traversing rightward through the 4,200-4,600 ft band, then cross a roughly 7,200 ft pass above Bird Lakes and descend into the Bird Lakes basin below Tupshin's east face (face starts ~7,600 ft). Most parties in July to September go in by the Devore Creek trail to the Bird Creek camp near 5,400-5,500 ft, then fight slide alder up to a basin camp around 5,800 ft; easy slopes lead to a ridge near 7,000 ft, then a descending traverse to the snow basin east of the summit block.

text.overview: A longer, harder technical line up Tupshin's east face, reached via a demanding cross-country approach from Company Creek over a pass above Bird Lakes; class 2-4 ledge scrambling leads to a short, poorly-protected 5.4-5.6 crux below the summit.
text.descent: Downclimb the summit pitch and upper class 4 terrain back through the ledge system, taking care around the crux flake/crack; parties have used a 30 m rope for the technical sections. Continue down the zigzagging ledges and the lower class 2-3 ramp back to the basin below the face, then reverse the cross-country traverse over the pass above Bird Lakes to Company Creek Trail.

text.overview: The north ridge is the rock route on Whistler, climbed from the highway shoulder shared with Cutthroat Peak. A climbers' trail drops into the open basin between the two peaks, then the route follows the ridge to the summit pyramid, mostly class 3 with some class 4 steps, over about 2,700 ft of gain. The ridge is exposed in places, and a fall would have serious consequences.
text.descent: Retrace the ridge. A short loose step is usually rappelled instead of downclimbed.
